summary: Adds a Flask search blueprint and a hardcoded Stripe key, changes item pagination, and loosens the Dockerfile, deploy script, CI step and lodash pin.

findings.title: Search query built from request input
findings.description: The search_items handler puts the q request argument into the SQL text with an f-string. Nothing escapes or binds the value. Any caller of the search endpoint can inject SQL and read or alter the items database. Pass q to cur.execute as a bound parameter with a question mark placeholder.
findings.suggested_change: cur.execute("SELECT id, name, price FROM items WHERE name = ?", (q,))
findings.problem: The search_items handler puts the q request argument into the SQL text with an f-string. Nothing escapes or binds the value.
findings.consequence: Any caller of the search endpoint can inject SQL and read or alter the items database.
findings.fix: Pass q to cur.execute as a bound parameter with a question mark placeholder.

findings.title: Pagination offset skips the first page
findings.description: The list_items handler now computes the offset as page times PAGE_SIZE. Page 1 therefore starts at row 20 instead of row 0. Clients never see the first 20 items, and the last page returns empty. Restore the offset to page minus one times PAGE_SIZE.
findings.problem: The list_items handler now computes the offset as page times PAGE_SIZE. Page 1 therefore starts at row 20 instead of row 0.
findings.consequence: Clients never see the first 20 items, and the last page returns empty.
findings.fix: Restore the offset to page minus one times PAGE_SIZE.

findings.title: Stripe secret key committed to source
findings.description: The config module hardcodes a value that matches the Stripe API key format. The commit stores the key in git history. Anyone with repository access can use the key against the shop's Stripe account. Revoke the key in Stripe and read it from an environment variable at runtime.
findings.problem: The config module hardcodes a value that matches the Stripe API key format. The commit stores the key in git history.
findings.consequence: Anyone with repository access can use the key against the shop's Stripe account.
findings.fix: Revoke the key in Stripe and read it from an environment variable at runtime.

findings.title: Container now runs as root
findings.description: The change removed the app user creation and the USER 10001 directive. The Flask server now runs as root inside the container. Any code execution bug in the app, such as the new search injection, gains root inside the container. Restore the useradd step and the USER 10001 directive before EXPOSE.
findings.problem: The change removed the app user creation and the USER 10001 directive. The Flask server now runs as root inside the container.
findings.consequence: Any code execution bug in the app, such as the new search injection, gains root inside the container.
findings.fix: Restore the useradd step and the USER 10001 directive before EXPOSE.

findings.title: Lodash downgraded to a vulnerable release
findings.description: The change pins lodash back from 4.18.1 to 4.17.15. That release has known command injection and prototype pollution flaws. Front-end code that uses template or path helpers inherits these flaws. Keep lodash at 4.18.1 in package.json and package-lock.json.
findings.problem: The change pins lodash back from 4.18.1 to 4.17.15. That release has known command injection and prototype pollution flaws.
findings.consequence: Front-end code that uses template or path helpers inherits these flaws.
findings.fix: Keep lodash at 4.18.1 in package.json and package-lock.json.

findings.title: Pull request title expanded into shell
findings.description: The new step expands the pull request title directly into the run script. A title with quotes or command substitution runs as shell. A pull request author can run arbitrary commands on the CI runner through the title. Pass the title through an env entry and echo the quoted variable.
findings.problem: The new step expands the pull request title directly into the run script. A title with quotes or command substitution runs as shell.
findings.consequence: A pull request author can run arbitrary commands on the CI runner through the title.
findings.fix: Pass the title through an env entry and echo the quoted variable.

findings.title: Base image unpinned to latest
findings.description: The change replaces the pinned python 3.12.7 slim image with python:latest. CI still tests against Python 3.12. Image builds can silently move to a newer Python than the one CI checks. Pin the base image to a specific Python release tag.
findings.problem: The change replaces the pinned python 3.12.7 slim image with python:latest. CI still tests against Python 3.12.
findings.consequence: Image builds can silently move to a newer Python than the one CI checks.
findings.fix: Pin the base image to a specific Python release tag.

findings.title: Unquoted path in recursive delete
findings.description: The change removed the quotes around DEPLOY_DIR in rm -rf. A DEPLOY_DIR with spaces splits into several paths. The deploy script can delete unrelated directories, such as the local app folder. Restore the quoted and guarded expansion.
findings.problem: The change removed the quotes around DEPLOY_DIR in rm -rf. A DEPLOY_DIR with spaces splits into several paths.
findings.consequence: The deploy script can delete unrelated directories, such as the local app folder.
findings.fix: Restore the quoted and guarded expansion.

findings.title: Changed endpoints have no tests
findings.description: The repository has no tests for the new search_items endpoint or the changed list_items pagination. Regressions like the pagination offset error reach users unnoticed. Add tests for search lookups and for the first page of list_items.
findings.problem: The repository has no tests for the new search_items endpoint or the changed list_items pagination.
findings.consequence: Regressions like the pagination offset error reach users unnoticed.
findings.fix: Add tests for search lookups and for the first page of list_items.

In order to execute raw query safely, prepared statement should be used. SQLAlchemy provides TextualSQL to easily used prepared statement with named parameters. For complex SQL composition, use SQL Expression Language or Schema Definition Language. In most cases, SQLAlchemy ORM will be a better option.

An attacker could use a SQL injection to steal or modify contents of the database. Instead, use a parameterized query which is available by default in most database engines. Alternatively, consider using the Django object-relational mappers (ORM) instead of raw SQL queries.
